bibl.title: Understanding gambling related harm: a proposed definition, conceptual framework, and taxonomy of harms

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: gambling related harm as a construct - whether it has a definition that can be operationalised, and what the field has been measuring in its place
span.quote: Whilst there is no single internationally agreed-upon definition of harm in relation to gambling, there are consistent patterns of interpretation throughout the literature that suggest some degree of convergence in the understanding of gambling-harm. Unlike indicators of gambling disorders or problematic behaviours, measures that specifically target gambling harm are under-developed.

span.label: what would a definition of gambling related harm have to do to be measurable from a public health perspective, and what taxonomy of harms would operationalise it
span.quote: However the absence of a detailed and explicit definition, with an accompanying conceptual model, makes it difficult to operationalize the concept and thereby measure the impacts or severity of harm experienced [1], and this deficit separates gambling from other public health issues to its detriment.

span.label: a functional definition of gambling related harm, a conceptual framework crossing three social levels with three temporal categories, and a taxonomy of specific harms built to be turned into measures
span.quote: Any initial or exacerbated adverse consequence due to an engagement with gambling that leads to a decrement to the health or wellbeing of an individual, family unit, community or population.

span.label: critique
span.quote: The current measurements used are inappropriate and insufficient, being most typically proxies of harm that come from gambling behaviour prevalence measures or unsystematic explorations of harms within the context of specific research studies. These approaches lack content validity, construct validity or both.

span.label: a public health field with no agreed definition of its central harm, measuring it by proxies drawn from a diagnostic category that is not the same thing
span.quote: Public health approaches to gambling in terms of prevention and treatment of problems with gambling make reference to harm minimisation. However, this term is somewhat ambiguous due to the lack of: (a) a consistent definition of gambling related harm, (b) conceptualisation of the breadth and experience of harm, and (c) an appropriate means of measuring harm.

span.label: four methodologies combined - literature review, focus groups and interviews with treatment professionals, interviews with people who gamble and affected others, and analysis of public forum posts - coded by grounded theory into a taxonomy
span.term: four methodologies combined - literature review, focus groups and interviews with treatment professionals, interviews with people who gamble and affected others, and analysis of public forum posts - coded by grounded theory into a taxonomy
span.quote: A conceptual framework links discrete concepts based on multiple theories and is seen as an impetus in the development of theory [14].

span.label: **THE TERM IS INTUITIVE AND THAT IS THE PROBLEM.** `Harm is a term that is IMMEDIATELY INTUITIVE, implying damage and adverse consequences. However, THE ASSUMPTION THAT IT IS UNNECESSARY TO DEFINE THE TERM PRECISELY in relation to gambling IS MISTAKEN`
span.quote: Harm is a term that is immediately intuitive, implying damage and adverse consequences. However, the assumption that it is unnecessary to define the term precisely in relation to gambling is mistaken.

span.label: and without a definition there is nothing to operationalise: `the absence of a detailed and explicit definition, with an accompanying conceptual model, MAKES IT DIFFICULT TO OPERATIONALIZE THE CONCEPT and thereby MEASURE the impacts or severity of harm`
span.quote: However the absence of a detailed and explicit definition, with an accompanying conceptual model, makes it difficult to operationalize the concept and thereby measure the impacts or severity of harm experienced [1], and this deficit separates gambling from other public health issues to its detriment.

span.label: **SO THE FIELD MEASURED SOMETHING ELSE.** `Unlike indicators of gambling disorders or problematic behaviours, measures that specifically target gambling harm are UNDER-DEVELOPED ... this reflects an emphasis on DIAGNOSIS OR SCREENING for problem gambling; RATHER THAN on measuring the range of negative outcomes`
span.quote: Whilst there is no single internationally agreed-upon definition of harm in relation to gambling, there are consistent patterns of interpretation throughout the literature that suggest some degree of convergence in the understanding of gambling-harm. Unlike indicators of gambling disorders or problematic behaviours, measures that specifically target gambling harm are under-developed.

span.label: with the consequence stated in psychometric terms: the current measures are `most typically PROXIES of harm that come from gambling behaviour prevalence measures or unsystematic explorations ... These approaches LACK CONTENT VALIDITY, CONSTRUCT VALIDITY OR BOTH`
span.quote: The current measurements used are inappropriate and insufficient, being most typically proxies of harm that come from gambling behaviour prevalence measures or unsystematic explorations of harms within the context of specific research studies. These approaches lack content validity, construct validity or both.

span.label: **THE TWO DEFINITIONS IN FORCE FAIL DIFFERENTLY.** Queensland `limit harm to occurring ONLY FROM PROBLEMATIC GAMBLING` and reads as `a PRODUCT-SAFETY PARADIGM ... INCONSISTENT WITH A SOCIAL MODEL OF HEALTH`; New Zealand's is broader and adds the insight `that gambling can EXACERBATE, AS WELL AS GENERATE harms`
span.quote: However, they limit harm to occurring only from problematic gambling and in describing safety and risk in relation to the product, the Queensland definition would appear to be focused on a product-safety paradigm of evaluating the hazard involved in consumption of commercial gambling which is inconsistent with a social model of health.

span.label: and both were judged unusable for the purpose that matters: `critical of both definitions for being TOO VAGUE TO BE USEFUL FOR OPERATIONALIZING the concept of gambling harm FOR THE PURPOSE OF MEASUREMENT`
span.quote: Neal et al [1] were critical of both definitions for being too vague to be useful for operationalizing the concept of gambling harm for the purpose of measurement. Similar limitations were later noted by Currie et al [4].

span.label: **THE PROPOSED DEFINITION IS ENGINEERED CLAUSE BY CLAUSE AND THE REASONS ARE GIVEN.** It `clearly delineates harm AS AN OUTCOME, allowing the focus to be on CONSEQUENCES RATHER THAN CAUSES OR SYMPTOMS`, explicitly separated from behaviour categorisation, clinical diagnosis, risk factors and environment
span.quote: Firstly, the definition clearly delineates harm as an outcome, allowing the focus to be on consequences rather than causes or symptoms of harmful gambling. It is explicit in separating this from related, but different, issues such as categorisations of behaviour of gambling, clinical diagnosis, risk factors or the environment in which gambling occurs.

span.label: and one word is defended on its own: `The use of the word DECREMENT captures BOTH THE GENERATION AND EXACERBATION of harm related to health and wellbeing, and is consistent with health state valuation calculation methodologies`
span.quote: The use of the word ‘decrement’ captures both the generation and exacerbation of harm related to health and wellbeing, and is consistent with health state valuation calculation methodologies.

span.label: **The paper declines to make its definition capture what it has just documented.** The data showed subjectivity and complex interrelation between harms, and `capturing this subjectivity and complexity WAS DETERMINED NOT TO BE THE ROLE OF A FUNCTIONAL DEFINITION` - a stated trade of fidelity for measurability
span.quote: However, capturing this subjectivity and complexity was determined not to be the role of a functional definition. The critical function for the definition was its ability to be operationalised in a way that gambling related harm could be measured consistent with other public health issues.

span.label: **the framework is explicitly not causal** - `The framework DOES NOT ATTEMPT TO CAPTURE CAUSAL SEQUENCES OR PATHWAYS of harms, this would only be possible using a prospective longitudinal methodology`
span.quote: The framework does not attempt to capture causal sequences or pathways of harms, this would only be possible using a prospective longitudinal methodology.

span.label: and the taxonomy's temporal placements are not generalisable: the categories `represent the temporal sequence WHERE THEY WERE IDENTIFIED WITHIN THE DATA, however this data IS NOT REPRESENTATIVE AND CANNOT BE GENERALISED. THE SUBJECTIVE NATURE OF A THRESHOLD MAKES GENERALISATION INAPPROPRIATE`
span.quote: The subjective nature of a threshold makes generalisation inappropriate and as such it is seen more of a reflection of experiences identified with a harm within

span.label: **the items are deliberately broad, and the generalisation is one-way** - `The items ... represent BROAD RATHER THAN SPECIFIC HARMS to facilitate the operationalisation of measures`, each individual experience checked as captured by a generalised item. `lied to my mates` becomes `Dishonest communication within relationships`
span.quote: The items listed within each of the taxonomies represent broad rather than specific harms to facilitate the operationalisation of measures of harm in future studies. On completion of the taxonomies each identified harm within the data was checked against the items to ensure the individual experience was captured in the generalised items.

span.label: and attribution is conceded at the end: `the harms outlined in this study CAN OCCUR DUE TO ENGAGEMENT IN OTHER BEHAVIOURS and can be exacerbated by the influence of COMORBIDITIES or existing dysfunction`
span.quote: It is important to caveat that the harms outlined in this study can occur due to engagement in other behaviours and can be exacerbated by the influence of comorbidities or existing dysfunction.

span.label: the disease model is adapted to gambling so that harm spreads from the person who gambles to family, friends and community, with that person as the index case rather than the source
span.quote: Consistent with the public health approach and the adaption of a disease model to understand gambling, a clear theme of the contagion of harm from the individual to family and friends, and then community emerged, noting that the person who gambles is the index case and not the source.

span.label: framing gambling harm as a public health matter broadens the focus from the individual gambler to the population
span.quote: This is an important broadening of focus that assists in addressing gambling related harm from a public health perspective.

span.label: gathering harm data by four separate methodologies - literature, professionals, people who gamble and affected others, and public forum posts
span.note: eliminates: a catalogue shaped by one vantage point; treatment professionals see crisis and legacy harms, and the general harms were `less significant in the early data` until participants were asked to expand on them · outcome: partial
span.quote: A conceptual framework links discrete concepts based on multiple theories and is seen as an impetus in the development of theory [14].

span.label: checking every individual harm in the data against the generalised taxonomy items after the taxonomy was written
span.note: eliminates: a taxonomy that looks complete because the cases that do not fit were never re-read against it · outcome: held
span.quote: The items listed within each of the taxonomies represent broad rather than specific harms to facilitate the operationalisation of measures of harm in future studies. On completion of the taxonomies each identified harm within the data was checked against the items to ensure the individual experience was captured in the generalised items.

span.label: requiring the classifications to be mutually exclusive while allowing the temporal categories to be crossed
span.note: eliminates: double counting within a dimension, without forcing a harm to occur at only one point in time - `a harm that occurs in the general harm temporal category could ALSO occur during a crisis or as a legacy harm` · outcome: held
span.quote: Consistent with the guidelines for creating a taxonomy, the division of entities into classifications were mutually exclusive, yet they can cross categorical boundaries. That is, a harm that occurs in the general harm temporal category could also occur during a crisis or as a legacy harm.

span.label: gambling harm
span.quote: Whilst there is no single internationally agreed-upon definition of harm in relation to gambling, there are consistent patterns of interpretation throughout the literature that suggest some degree of convergence in the understanding of gambling-harm. Unlike indicators of gambling disorders or problematic behaviours, measures that specifically target gambling harm are under-developed.

span.label: harm minimisation
span.quote: Public health approaches to gambling in terms of prevention and treatment of problems with gambling make reference to harm minimisation. However, this term is somewhat ambiguous due to the lack of: (a) a consistent definition of gambling related harm, (b) conceptualisation of the breadth and experience of harm, and (c) an appropriate means of measuring harm.

span.label: proxies
span.quote: The current measurements used are inappropriate and insufficient, being most typically proxies of harm that come from gambling behaviour prevalence measures or unsystematic explorations of harms within the context of specific research studies. These approaches lack content validity, construct validity or both.

span.label: PGSI
span.quote: This is particularly true of gambling behaviour measures such as the PGSI or monetary loss. Whilst these measures have an important contribution to our understanding and examination of gambling as a behaviour, as a health behaviour they should be considered as a risk factor and not as an outcome.

span.label: outcome
span.quote: Firstly, the definition clearly delineates harm as an outcome, allowing the focus to be on consequences rather than causes or symptoms of harmful gambling. It is explicit in separating this from related, but different, issues such as categorisations of behaviour of gambling, clinical diagnosis, risk factors or the environment in which gambling occurs.

span.label: Queensland definition
span.quote: The Queensland definition describes harm as a ‘range of adverse consequences’, in which ‘the safety or wellbeing of gambling consumers or their family or friends are placed at risk’ and/or negative impacts extending to the broader community. In describing harm as a set of impacts and consequences, the Queensland definition is clear that gambling harms are the outcome of problematic gambling, rather than problematic gambling itself.

span.label: New Zealand
span.quote: The New Zealand 2003 Gambling Act definition is broader, describing harm as ‘any kind of harm or distress arising from, or caused or exacerbated by, a person’s gambling’. This definition includes psychological or emotional impacts of gambling, as well as presumably more concrete forms of harm, such as financial loss.

span.label: decrement
span.quote: The use of the word ‘decrement’ captures both the generation and exacerbation of harm related to health and wellbeing, and is consistent with health state valuation calculation methodologies.

span.label: legacy harms
span.quote: Legacy harms related to those harms that continue to occur (or emerge) even if the person’s engagement with gambling ceases through changes in their own or someone else’s behaviour, but may also be experienced if a person continues to gamble. The label was chosen to capture the ongoing impact of harm, and to highlight that harm does not cease with the behaviour.

span.label: conceptual framework
span.quote: A conceptual framework links discrete concepts based on multiple theories and is seen as an impetus in the development of theory [14].

span.label: taxonomy
span.quote: Consistent with the guidelines for creating a taxonomy, the division of entities into classifications were mutually exclusive, yet they can cross categorical boundaries. That is, a harm that occurs in the general harm temporal category could also occur during a crisis or as a legacy harm.

span.quote: The subjective nature of a threshold makes generalisation inappropriate and as such it is seen more of a reflection of experiences identified with a harm within

span.label: comorbidities
span.quote: It is important to caveat that the harms outlined in this study can occur due to engagement in other behaviours and can be exacerbated by the influence of comorbidities or existing dysfunction.

span.quote: The Queensland definition describes harm as a ‘range of adverse consequences’, in which ‘the safety or wellbeing of gambling consumers or their family or friends are placed at risk’ and/or negative impacts extending to the broader community. In describing harm as a set of impacts and consequences, the Queensland definition is clear that gambling harms are the outcome of problematic gambling, rather than problematic gambling itself.

span.label: `gambling related harm` (proposed here) - `Any initial or exacerbated adverse consequence due to an engagement with gambling that leads to A DECREMENT to the health or wellbeing of an individual, family unit, community or population`
span.quote: Any initial or exacerbated adverse consequence due to an engagement with gambling that leads to a decrement to the health or wellbeing of an individual, family unit, community or population.

span.label: `legacy harm` - harm that continues or emerges after engagement with gambling ceases; the label exists to mark that harm does not end with the behaviour
span.quote: Legacy harms related to those harms that continue to occur (or emerge) even if the person’s engagement with gambling ceases through changes in their own or someone else’s behaviour, but may also be experienced if a person continues to gamble. The label was chosen to capture the ongoing impact of harm, and to highlight that harm does not cease with the behaviour.

span.label: `harm` in ordinary use - `immediately intuitive, implying damage and adverse consequences`, and that intuitiveness is precisely why it went undefined
span.quote: Harm is a term that is immediately intuitive, implying damage and adverse consequences. However, the assumption that it is unnecessary to define the term precisely in relation to gambling is mistaken.

span.label: `harm` - SLIDING BETWEEN THE CAUSE AND THE EFFECT: `the term harm is often USED INTERCHANGEABLY TO REFER TO THE BEHAVIOUR - NOT JUST THE CONSEQUENCE`. One word covering the gambling and the damage it does, which makes any claim that one produces the other unfalsifiable.
span.quote: To add further uncertainty, the term harm is often used interchangeably to refer to the behaviour - not just the consequence
